title: University of Maryland - CS13 Bowtie
description: Stand-alone bow-tie for University of Maryland - CS13 (heart failure).

leftContent.intro: The nurse is caring for a 68-year-old client who is admitted to the medical unit from an outpatient clinic.

tabs.title: Admission Notes
tabs.content: Day 1 1100:Client reports that his primary care provider sent him to the hospital after his follow-up appointment today because of a nagging cough, pink-tinged sputum, and difficulty “catching” his breath. States he is sleeping in a recliner because of difficulty breathing when lying down in bed. Reports lack of appetite, thirst, and getting up twice a night to urinate. States feeling “worried” about his health. No known drug allergies.

tabs.title: History and Physical
tabs.content:
CardiacRegular rhythm, tachycardia; 4+ pitting pedal and pretibial edema
RespiratoryUnlabored; crackles in bases bilaterally
NeurologicOriented to time, place, person, and situation; anxious
GastrointestinalAbdomen soft, nontender; bowel sounds active
SkinWarm, dry, intact
GenitourinaryFrequent urination, small amounts, clear yellow, no foul odor

tabs.title: Vital Signs
tabs.content:
1100
T37°C (98.6°F)
P110
RR22
BP170/110
Pulse oximetry reading93% on room air
Weight97.7 kg (215 lb)

question.stem: Complete the diagram by dragging from the choices below to specify what condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take to address that condition, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess the client’s progress.
question.explanation:
A nagging cough, pink-tinged sputum, and orthopnea are symptoms of worsening heart failure. Appropriate actions are an IV diuretic and a fluid restriction, and weight and lung sounds show whether the interventions are effective.
There is no indication of infection, so IV antibiotics and WBC monitoring are not appropriate. Normal saline is contraindicated because of the fluid overload. A Foley catheter is not indicated because the client is voiding. The pulse oximetry reading and heart sounds are stable.
